name: Brown Button Cap
guideText: Can appear on any tile.

name: Puffball
guideText: Bursts into spores when picked.

name: Shelf Fungus
guideText: Grows on rocks.

name: Moonlight Morel
guideText: Night only.

name: Ink Cap
guideText: Melts into ink if left unpicked for a day.

name: Foxfire Button
guideText: A small cap that glows green at night; the first sign of Glow in the ground.

name: Turkey Tail
guideText: Grows on fallen logs. Colour-banded shelf fungi grow in overlapping fans on dead wood.

name: Earthstar
guideText: A round spore sac sits inside star-like outer rays that split open.

name: Ghost Fungus
guideText: Night only. A pale woodland fungus known for its eerie greenish glow.

name: Cave Truffle
guideText: Veiled; tap the mound to uncover.

name: Starlight Bonnet
guideText: Night only.

name: Amethyst Deceiver
guideText: A vivid purple woodland mushroom that gives the forest floor an otherworldly accent.

name: Ancient Sporecrown
guideText: Night only, during rain. Only one can exist in a forest at a time.

name: Clover
guideText: Soft carpets of flowering leaves that attract pollinators. Can appear on any tile.

name: Primrose
guideText: Pale yellow, the first flower of spring. Likes lush grass.

name: Forget-me-not
guideText: Tiny blue flowers that come up where flowers grow thick.

name: Poppy
guideText: A bright red poppy, happiest among other flowers.

name: Snowdrop
guideText: Nodding white bells that push up between little crystals.

name: Columbine
guideText: Spurred violet flowers that seem to glow at dusk.

name: Bleeding Heart
guideText: Arching stems carry distinctive heart-shaped pink flowers.

name: Moss Rose
guideText: Grows between crystals.

name: Sunpetal
guideText: Daytime only.

name: Dandelion
guideText: Seeds can drift to a random nearby tile.

name: Hollow Root
guideText: A knot of old roots pushed up through the fae mist.

name: Foxglove
guideText: Tall spires of tubular flowers that bring height and colour to meadow edges.

name: Moonflower
guideText: Night only.

name: Ghost Orchid
guideText: A rare, pale orchid with an almost floating appearance.

name: Heartwood Sapling
guideText: Only one per forest. Grows into a permanent landmark tree.

name: Water Reed
guideText: Shallow water only. Grows in clusters.

name: Mystery Seed
guideText: Plant it: grows into a random plant, or rarely a Sproutling.

name: Pebble Geode
guideText: Buried; tap soil to dig. Can appear on any tile.

name: Mossy Geode
guideText: Buried.

name: Rootbound Geode
guideText: Buried; wrapped in roots.

name: Deep Geode
guideText: Buried.

name: Glimmering Geode
guideText: Buried.

name: Ancient Heartstone
guideText: Buried; only one per forest at a time. Only geode that can hold Legendary materials.

name: Quartz

name: Flint

howFound: Cracked from: Pebble Geode

name: Agate

use.text: Crush into soil: +5 Bloom on a tile for 24h

howFound: Cracked from: Pebble Geode, Mossy Geode, Rootbound Geode

name: Pyrite

use.text: Crush into soil: +5 Spore on a tile for 24h

howFound: Cracked from: Pebble Geode, Mossy Geode
guideText: Looks valuable, isn't.

name: Jasper

use.text: Crush into soil: +8 Shimmer on a tile for 24h

howFound: Cracked from: Pebble Geode, Mossy Geode, Rootbound Geode

name: Malachite

use.text: Crush into soil: +8 Spore on a tile for 24h

howFound: Cracked from: Mossy Geode, Rootbound Geode

name: Emerald

use.text: Crush into soil: +8 Bloom on a tile for 24h

howFound: Cracked from: Mossy Geode, Rootbound Geode

name: Amethyst

use.text: Crush into soil: +8 Spirit on a tile for 24h

howFound: Cracked from: Mossy Geode, Deep Geode

name: Amber

use.text: Crush into soil: +8 Verdure on a tile for 24h

howFound: Cracked from: Rootbound Geode
guideText: Sometimes holds a tiny trapped bug.

name: Moonstone

use.text: Crush into soil: +8 Glow on a tile for 24h

howFound: Cracked from: Deep Geode, Glimmering Geode

name: Garnet

use.text: Crush into soil: +12 Bloom on a tile for 48h

howFound: Cracked from: Deep Geode, Glimmering Geode

name: Topaz

use.text: Crush into soil: +12 Verdure on a tile for 48h

howFound: Cracked from: Rootbound Geode, Deep Geode

name: Fluorite

use.text: Crush into soil: +12 Glow on a tile for 48h

howFound: Cracked from: Deep Geode, Glimmering Geode
guideText: Glows faintly in your inventory.

name: Sapphire

use.text: Crush into soil: +12 Spore on a tile for 48h

howFound: Cracked from: Deep Geode

name: Star Sapphire

use.text: Crush into soil: +15 Spore and +15 Glow on a tile for 48h

howFound: Cracked from: Deep Geode, Glimmering Geode, Ancient Heartstone

name: Opal

use.text: Crush into soil: +15 Bloom and +15 Glow on a tile for 48h

howFound: Cracked from: Glimmering Geode, Ancient Heartstone

name: Bioluminite

howFound: Cracked from: Glimmering Geode, Ancient Heartstone

name: Spore Crystal

guideText: Mushrooms love it.

name: Heartstone Core

use.text: Set into a tile: permanently +10 to all six stats there

howFound: Cracked from: Ancient Heartstone

name: Moonfall Shard

use.text: Use on a creature source item: guarantees the next creature found is a Glimmer

howFound: Cracked from: Ancient Heartstone

name: Forest Fruit
howFound: Grows on a Fruit Tree landmark
guideText: Sweet red fruit. Wanderers and the Old Log both love it.

name: Meadow Daisy
guideText: Small white daisies that open towards the light.

name: Velvet Shank
guideText: Velvety stems in a mossy cluster, damp with spores.

name: Ember Cap
guideText: Its gills hold a faint orange light.

name: Honeybell
guideText: Golden, bell-shaped blooms that bead with sweet nectar.

name: Feather Fern
guideText: Fronds so fine they move with your breath.

name: Glassbell
guideText: A flower like thin crystal, ringing faintly in the wind.

name: Veil Cap
guideText: A pale cap that seems to fade when you look straight at it.

name: Ring Morel
guideText: The morel every fairy ring grows around.

name: Lantern Flower
guideText: A little bell of light that sways in the dark.

name: Starwort
guideText: Night only. Star-shaped flowers that only open under the night sky.

name: Buttercup
guideText: Glossy yellow cups that catch the sun.

name: Wild Rose
guideText: Thorny shrubs with fragrant blossoms and colourful rose hips.

name: Sun Lily
guideText: Daytime only. Opens wide at midday and closes by evening.

name: Dawn Peony
guideText: Petals the colour of the first light.

name: Greenheart Vine
guideText: A vine so green it almost glows.

name: Prism Rose
guideText: Its petals split the light like glass.

name: Wisp Cap
guideText: A pale little cap that trails a thread of mist.

name: Mistbell
guideText: Pale bells that ring without a sound.

name: Silver Ragwort
guideText: A hardy plant with soft, silvery foliage that catches the light.

name: Jewelweed
guideText: A delicate wildflower with jewel-like orange or yellow blooms and water-beading leaves.

name: Pearlroot
guideText: A low plant with pearlescent leaves and bead-like roots.

name: Glassreed
guideText: Clear, slender reeds that chime softly when brushed by the wind.

name: Prismbell
guideText: Translucent bell-shaped blooms split sunlight into tiny rainbow flecks.

name: Opal Fern
guideText: Silvery fronds flash pink, blue, and green as the viewing angle changes.

name: Rainbow Eucalyptus
guideText: A striking tree with naturally multicoloured, peeling bark.

name: Mirrorcap
guideText: Smooth silver caps reflect a blurred image of the surrounding grove.

name: Glimmerlace
guideText: Fine lace-like fungus threaded with iridescent droplets.

name: Opaline Shelf
guideText: Layered shelf fungus with opal colours shimmering along its edges.

name: Cornflower
guideText: Bright blue flowers that thrive in sunny, open ground.

name: Cosmos
guideText: Airy, daisy-like flowers on delicate stems, often in pink, white, and magenta.

name: Lupine
guideText: Upright flower spikes with densely packed pea-shaped blooms.

name: Anemone
guideText: Open, delicate flowers with dark centres and vivid petals.

name: Mooncup Blossom
guideText: Night only. A broad, pale flower that opens only beneath the moon.

name: Marigold
guideText: Cheerful orange pom-pom flowers that brighten in full sun.

name: Sweet Pea
guideText: Curling tendrils carry ruffled, sweet-scented blooms in soft pastels.

name: Lavender
guideText: Fragrant purple spikes that hum with visiting bees.

name: Sunfire Daisy
guideText: Daytime only. Its petals flicker gold and orange like a small, warm flame in the noon light.

name: Petalwhirl
guideText: Layer upon layer of petals turn slowly on the stem like a gentle pinwheel.

name: Stargrass
guideText: Fine blades are tipped with pinprick lights like stars scattered across the ground.

name: Lantern Lily
guideText: Drooping flowers shine like tiny paper lanterns.

name: Moonpetal
guideText: Night only. Cool-toned petals open at night and emit a gentle blue glow.

name: Foxfire Orchid
guideText: Night only. A pale orchid whose veins glow softly after dusk.

name: Honey Mushroom
guideText: A woodland mushroom that can produce a faint glow in its mycelium.

name: Jack-o'-Lantern Mushroom
guideText: An orange mushroom with bioluminescent gills that glow in darkness.

name: Bluebell Glowcap
guideText: Clusters of blue, bell-shaped caps illuminate nearby moss.

name: Nightlight Bracket
guideText: Night only. A shelf fungus with luminous rings that brighten as night falls.

name: Starspore
guideText: Tiny glowing mushrooms release drifting specks of light when disturbed.

name: Moonwort
guideText: A small, unusual fern-like plant with a delicate, ancient appearance.

name: Ghostpipe
guideText: A waxy, translucent-white woodland plant that lacks green chlorophyll.

name: White Sage
guideText: A silvery, aromatic plant associated with dry, open landscapes.

name: Ancestor's Lace
guideText: Delicate white flowers appear in rings around old stones.

name: Wispwillow
guideText: A small willow-like tree whose hanging leaves drift as if underwater.

name: Corpse Flower
guideText: A dramatic, rare flowering plant with an enormous bloom and powerful scent.

name: Veil Shank
guideText: A slender mushroom wrapped in a translucent veil of mist.

name: Wisp Puff
guideText: A pale puffball releases drifting, ghost-like clouds of spores.

name: Shaggy Inkcap
guideText: A tall white mushroom whose cap dissolves into dark ink as it matures.

name: Fly Agaric
guideText: A familiar red cap dotted with white warts, often found near trees.

name: Dead Man's Fingers
guideText: Dark, finger-like fungal fruiting bodies emerge from decaying wood.

name: Violet Webcap
guideText: A striking purple woodland mushroom with delicate veil-like webbing.

name: Stinkhorn
guideText: An unusual fungus with a distinctive shape and scent that attracts insects.

name: Morel
guideText: A prized spring mushroom with a deeply honeycombed cap.

name: Spore Lantern
guideText: A bulbous mushroom releases visible clouds of sparkling spores.

name: Crown Puffball
guideText: A round puffball splits into curled points like a tiny crown when mature.

name: Wood Sorrel
guideText: Clover-like leaves and small flowers carpet shady forest floors.

name: Wild Ginger
guideText: A low woodland groundcover with broad leaves and hidden flowers.

name: Hosta
guideText: Broad, overlapping leaves create lush mounds in shaded gardens.

name: Maidenhair Fern
guideText: Graceful fronds carry fine, fan-shaped leaflets and favour shade and moisture.

name: Ostrich Fern
guideText: Tall, feathery fronds unfurl in dramatic clusters in damp woodland.

name: Solomon's Seal
guideText: Arching stems carry paired leaves and dangling bell-shaped flowers.

name: Hellebore
guideText: A hardy woodland-edge perennial with nodding flowers and leathery leaves.

name: Canopy Bells
guideText: Small green flowers hang beneath large umbrella-like leaves.

name: Heartleaf Canopy
guideText: A lush broad-leaved plant forms miniature layers of living cover.

name: Green Elf Cup
guideText: A small cup fungus can stain nearby wood a vivid green.
